content: Ligand 1 is the azetidine-piperazinium host again, and ligand 2 is a rigid fused chromone-lactam (SA 2.73, 1 rotatable bond) with no activity - a crossover would mostly import that strained tricycle at random, so I will do a directed rebuild instead. Having already put an indazole on this exact scaffold at this exact anchor, repeating the operation with a different core gives a matched-scaffold comparison of chemotypes. Cut non-ring bond 11-12 to drop the protonated piperazine (which is what holds QED at 0.63 and LogP at -1.70) and graft carbazol-3-yl: a planar tricyclic aromatic with an NH donor, which is the cheapest structural mimic available of the anthrapyrazolone core of the reference JNK inhibitor SP600125, and also the core of the carbazole-carboxamide JNK series. It is a much larger, flatter, more distinctive graft than the indazole, so it tests both chemotype and planarity on a scaffold I already have a baseline for.
